subject: Post-demo qualification & guarded rollout plan for PayLane
messages:
From: Sam Hayes <sam.hayes@paylane.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emilia Ruiz <emilia@paylane.com>
Date: 2027-04-28T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick follow-up after demo — model choices + regression concerns

Hi Irene / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo today — appreciate the depth on latency and cost controls. A couple of things for the team as we evaluate Redwood for an initial pilot:

- Can you recommend which model families you think map best to our use case (payment-fraud signal enrichment + merchant support chat)? We care about precision for classification-ish prompts and consistent conversational tone for chat.
- We have an internal mandate to avoid surprises after model updates. What are your guarded rollout mechanics? How quickly can we pin a version if quality degrades?
- Please share any benchmark reports, a sample prompt set we can run, and a short checklist we should use during the trial.

If you can send an action plan and any materials, Emilia and I will review and reply with a timeline for the pilot.

Best,
Sam
Head of ML Product
PayLane

Attachments: none
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Hayes <sam.hayes@paylane.com>, Emilia Ruiz <emilia@paylane.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-29T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Quick follow-up after demo — model choices + regression concerns

Sam / Emilia — thanks for the clear asks, and glad the demo was useful. Long answer short: we recommend two paths (fast prototype vs. conservative production). Below is a concise plan + links.

1) Recommended model choices
- Prototype (fast): Llama-3-13B-quant (low-cost, quick iteration). Good for early prompt tuning and chat flow.
- Conservative (production): OPT-30B-std (strong precision on few-shot classification tasks w/ our inference optimizations). Slightly higher cost but more predictable underpinning for pinned versions.

2) Benchmarks & artifacts (links/attachments)
- Summary benchmark (latency / P95 / tokens-per-second): https://s3.redwood.ai/paylane/benchmarks/summary.html
- Eval pack (attachment): paylane_eval_pack_v1.zip — includes 150 labeled prompt pairs, expected outputs, and target quality gates.
- Prompt set (attachment): prompt_set_paylane.md — starter prompts for enrichment and chat, plus negative-case tests.

3) Regression guardrails & pinning mechanics
- Default: we serve a model alias (e.g., paylane-prod-v1) that we can map to specific model+weights.
- Pinning: within your Dedicated or Private deployment you can request an exact model hash pin; that takes effect within minutes and is reversible. We recommend 'soft pin' first (alias to exact variant) for two-week runway.
- Emergency rollback: our playbook (rollback_playbook.pdf attached) contains a one-click fallback to the previous verified variant plus a short-circuit policy that routes 100% traffic to the fallback within 3–5 minutes.

4) Quality monitoring
- We propose a nightly diff job that runs the eval pack against any candidate update and produces a differential report (delta precision / recall / hallucination rate). If delta exceeds thresholds we'll trigger a hold.

5) Proposed next steps (mutual action plan)
- I will share the eval pack and prompt set (attached).
- Marissa to follow with a 3-week pilot proposal and pricing.
- Engineering (aditya_rao) to confirm pinning SLA and any infra prep we need on your side.

Let us know what else you need. We can also sketch an A/B rollout if you want staged exposure for live traffic.

Cheers,
Irene Choi
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: paylane_eval_pack_v1.zip, prompt_set_paylane.md, rollback_playbook.pdf
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Sam Hayes <sam.hayes@paylane.com>, Emilia Ruiz <emilia@paylane.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-30T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Quick follow-up after demo — model choices + regression concerns

Sam / Emilia — quick technical note on pinning and rollback feasibility:

- Pinning to a model hash: supported on Hosted & Dedicated. For Private deployments we provide the same alias mechanics but the customer controls the image & weights; we provide the config and the one-click script.
- Time-to-pin: in Hosted/Dedicated we can alias within ~5 minutes in most cases; if the variant requires new GPU-specific kernels (rare) it can take up to ~45 minutes while the runtime compiles optimized kernels. We flag that during the pre-flight.
- Cost considerations: pinning itself doesn’t change inference cost, but productionizing a heavier model variant (OPT-30B-std) will raise per-token cost ~2–2.5x vs Llama-3-13B-quant. We can run a cost projection for your expected QPS.

Operational suggestion: start with Llama-3-13B-quant for prompt tuning and nightly diffing. When you hit the quality gate we recommend a staged push to OPT-30B-std behind a canary for a 48–72 hour window. If any regression metric moves more than 2–3% we auto-roll to the previous pinned version.

I can pull together the quick pre-flight checklist if you want — will add infra items (IP allowlist, quota, key rotation).

—Aditya
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
